git grep -E gives \b no meaning, so the pattern matches nothing and exits 1. That reads like a genuine no-match, and a tool answering false costs more than one that errors. git grep -P in single quotes is the fix. Separately, printf, echo -e and $'...' substitute a real 0x08 byte before git runs, which defeats -E, -F and -P alike, and quoting a heredoc delimiter does not protect a Python string literal against the same substitution. Full measurements on git/Q/Why does git grep -E report no matches for a word-boundary pattern?.

Every link inside a personalised email carries an identifier for whoever received it. The wayfinder links in the Latent Space newsletter are substack.com/redirect/...?j=<token> URLs whose parameter identifies Person/codekiln's subscription, so following one registers a click on their account and writing one into a page publishes it. This is general rather than a fact about one newsletter. The real destination can often be decoded out of the payload offline instead, which is how https://www.latent.space/p/wayfinder-skill was recovered with no request.

A layout pass and a content pass are different passes. This seat reformatted the display's one item at 15:32, measured it clean for hard wraps and tables, and only at 15:43 saw that the item was 121 words of forensics behind a one-word decision — and that three of its counts were stale. No formatting check can see a stale number. The repair is a check date on every line, which is the one field that makes staleness visible to a formatting pass.
